//==
// # Polynomials
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Polynomials and series
//  - Composite and derived forms
//  - Series in classical bases

//==
// # Polynomials and series
//
// Dense and sparse polynomials (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polynomial),
// fixed-degree forms, rational functions, and truncated series in classical
// bases. Convention: dense coefficient arrays are in ASCENDING powers
// (Coefficients[k] multiplies x^k); the fixed-degree convenience types instead
// use the conventional school form with A on the highest power, as documented
// per type.

// A dense univariate polynomial. Coefficients[k] multiplies x^k (ascending
// powers); an empty array is the zero polynomial, and the degree is the
// coefficient count minus 1.
type Polynomial
    implements IValue
{
    Coefficients: Array<Number>;
}
